note: Instructional benchmark suite. Expanded 2026-07 to test whether the instructional architecture GENERALIZES across a broad range of writing situations (genres/communicative purposes, writing elements, proficiency levels incl. ELL, and student states) rather than optimizing for the original 32 cases. TC01-TC32 original; TC33-TC66 diversity expansion.

cases.name: Misunderstanding the assignment
cases.assignment: Argue whether year-round school would help students learn.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Help the student answer the actual question with a clear position.
cases.initial_draft: School is important. Kids need to learn a lot of things like math and reading. Teachers work hard. School helps you get a job later.
expected_issues: does not address the year-round question

cases.name: Answering a broader question than asked
cases.assignment: Argue whether social media harms teen friendships specifically.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Keep the essay scoped to the assignment.
cases.initial_draft: Social media is bad for society. It spreads misinformation, hurts democracy, and makes people addicted to their phones. It changes how everyone lives.
expected_issues: scope too broad; not about teen friendships

cases.name: No thesis
cases.assignment: Argue whether homework should be limited.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Form a clear thesis.
cases.initial_draft: Homework. Students get a lot of homework. Some people like it and some people don't. There are many opinions about homework.
expected_issues: no position/thesis
avoid_behaviors: writing a thesis for the student

cases.name: Topic mistaken for thesis
cases.assignment: Argue a position on school uniforms.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Distinguish topic from thesis.
cases.initial_draft: This essay is about school uniforms. I will talk about school uniforms and whether they are good or bad.
expected_issues: announces topic, not a claim
avoid_behaviors: accepting the topic sentence as a thesis

cases.name: Vague thesis
cases.assignment: Argue whether cities should ban cars downtown.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Sharpen a vague thesis into a precise claim.
cases.initial_draft: Banning cars downtown could be good in some ways but it also has some problems, so it is a complicated issue with different sides.
expected_issues: too vague; no committed position

cases.name: Adequate thesis
cases.assignment: Argue whether standardized tests should be required for college.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Move from an adequate thesis to support.
cases.initial_draft: Colleges should stop requiring standardized tests because the scores track family income more than a student's ability to succeed.
expected_issues: thesis adequate; next is support/evidence

cases.name: Strong thesis that should not be over-taught
cases.assignment: Argue a position on remote work.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Avoid unnecessary intervention on strong writing.
cases.initial_draft: Remote work does not erode collaboration; it exposes how much of our old collaboration was proximity mistaken for teamwork. When presence is no longer automatic, teams must design connection deliberately—and the deliberate version is usually better.
expected_issues: thesis is strong

cases.name: Evidence without explanation
cases.assignment: Argue whether phones should be banned in class.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Connect evidence to the claim through explanation.
cases.initial_draft: Phones hurt learning. A study found that students who used phones in class scored 20% lower on tests. Another survey said 60% of teachers see phones as a distraction.
expected_issues: evidence dropped in without interpretation

cases.name: Explanation without evidence
cases.assignment: Argue whether zoos are ethical.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Ground reasoning in evidence.
cases.initial_draft: Zoos are unethical because keeping animals in captivity is wrong. It just feels cruel to lock animals up when they should be free. Everyone knows this is true.
expected_issues: assertion/reasoning with no evidence

cases.name: Irrelevant evidence
cases.assignment: Argue whether recess should be longer.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Judge evidence relevance to the claim.
cases.initial_draft: Recess should be longer. Exercise is good for your heart and reduces the risk of heart disease later in life. Also, the school cafeteria food is not very healthy.
expected_issues: evidence not relevant to 'longer recess helps learning/behavior'

cases.name: Weak paragraph unity
cases.assignment: Explain the causes of the American Revolution.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Build paragraph unity.
cases.initial_draft: Taxes were a big cause of the revolution. The colonists were mad about taxes without representation. Also George Washington was a great general. The Boston Tea Party happened. Britain was far away across the ocean.
expected_issues: sentences don't serve one governing idea
avoid_behaviors: reordering the paragraph for the student

cases.name: Missing topic sentence
cases.assignment: Analyze a theme in a novel.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Establish a topic sentence.
cases.initial_draft: In chapter three, the main character gives away his coat. Later he shares his food. At the end he stays behind so others can escape. These are all in the book.
expected_issues: no topic sentence stating the paragraph's claim

cases.name: Effective topic sentence
cases.assignment: Analyze a theme in a poem.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Recognize a working topic sentence; move to development.
cases.initial_draft: The poem's repeated images of winter cold quietly measure the distance between the father's love and the son's understanding of it.
expected_issues: topic sentence works; needs development

cases.name: Poor organization
cases.assignment: Argue whether school should start later.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Improve whole-essay organization.
cases.initial_draft: School should start later. Buses would need new schedules. Teens need more sleep. Also parents might have trouble with work. Sleep affects grades. In conclusion later is better. Sports practice could be an issue.
expected_issues: ideas out of logical order

cases.name: Weak transition
cases.assignment: Argue whether junk food should be taxed.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Make relationships between ideas explicit.
cases.initial_draft: Junk food causes health problems. Taxes reduce how much people buy something. Kids eat a lot of junk food. A tax would raise money for schools.
expected_issues: missing/weak relationships between sentences
avoid_behaviors: inserting transition words for the student

cases.name: Forced/unnecessary transition
cases.assignment: Explain how photosynthesis works.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Use transitions only where relationships need signaling.
cases.initial_draft: Firstly, plants have leaves. Secondly, leaves are green. Furthermore, moreover, in addition, plants also need water. Consequently, therefore, plants make food.
expected_issues: mechanical, stacked transition words

cases.name: Introduction with no context
cases.assignment: Explain the significance of the printing press.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Provide reader context in the introduction.
cases.initial_draft: It changed everything. People could finally do it faster and cheaper. This was a huge deal and it mattered a lot for the whole world.
expected_issues: no subject/context; reader lost

cases.name: Effective introduction
cases.assignment: Argue a position on universal basic income.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Recognize an effective intro; move forward.
cases.initial_draft: Every automation debate eventually arrives at the same anxious question: what happens to people when the work runs out? Universal basic income is the boldest answer on offer—not a safety net but a floor. This essay argues that a floor, not a net, is what a post-automation economy actually requires.
expected_issues: intro effective

cases.name: Conclusion that merely repeats
cases.assignment: Argue whether video games cause violence.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Make the conclusion do communicative work.
cases.initial_draft: In conclusion, video games do not cause violence. As I said, studies don't show a link. As I stated earlier, most gamers are not violent. So in conclusion video games do not cause violence.
expected_issues: restates without adding significance

cases.name: Sentence-level confusion
cases.assignment: Explain your favorite hobby.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Clarify a confusing sentence.
cases.initial_draft: The thing about when I do the hobby which is skateboarding because it makes me feel and the tricks are hard but worth doing them even falling down a lot happens.
expected_issues: syntax breakdown; no clear assertion

cases.name: Unclear pronoun reference
cases.assignment: Explain a conflict between two characters.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Clarify pronoun reference.
cases.initial_draft: When John talked to his father about his car, he told him that he had ruined it and that he would have to pay him back for it, which made him angry.
expected_issues: ambiguous 'he/him/it' references
avoid_behaviors: rewriting the sentence for the student

cases.name: Overly colloquial writing
cases.assignment: Write a formal argument about renewable energy.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Adjust tone for a formal audience.
cases.initial_draft: Ok so basically renewable energy is super important lol. Fossil fuels are trash and kinda ruining the planet ngl. We gotta switch or we're totally doomed tbh.
expected_issues: tone unsuited to a formal audience
avoid_behaviors: rewriting into formal prose for the student

cases.name: Sophisticated writing with a subtle conceptual problem
cases.assignment: Analyze whether meritocracy is fair.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Surface a subtle reasoning gap.
cases.initial_draft: Meritocracy is fair because it rewards the talented and hardworking. Since the successful are demonstrably talented and hardworking—otherwise they would not be successful—the system evidently rewards the right people, proving that it works as intended.
expected_issues: circular reasoning: success defines merit
avoid_behaviors: over-editing sentences instead of the reasoning

cases.name: Student resistance
cases.assignment: Argue whether cellphones help or hurt learning.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Maintain supportive instructional direction under resistance.
cases.initial_draft: Phones are fine. I don't see why this even matters. My essay is done and it's good enough.
responses: I already said phones are fine. Why do I need a thesis? This is dumb.
expected_issues: resistance; no developed position

cases.name: Student asks the AI to write the answer
cases.assignment: Argue whether public transit should be free.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Preserve student authorship (anti-coauthoring).
cases.initial_draft: Public transit and money and cities. I don't know how to start.
responses: Can you just write the thesis for me? Just give me a good one I can use.
expected_issues: request to co-author

cases.name: Very short response
cases.assignment: Argue whether pets should be allowed in classrooms.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Elicit a performable act from a minimal response.
cases.initial_draft: Pets are good.
expected_issues: minimal; no claim or reasoning

cases.name: Student confused by terminology
cases.assignment: Argue whether school lunches should be free.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Define canonical terms in accessible language.
cases.initial_draft: School lunches cost money for some kids and that is hard for families.
responses: What's a thesis? I don't know what that word means.
expected_issues: needs the term 'thesis' taught plainly

cases.name: Student successfully performs the requested act
cases.assignment: Argue whether social media harms teen friendships.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Consolidate and advance after success.
cases.initial_draft: Social media is both good and bad for friendships.
responses: Social media mostly harms close teen friendships, because it replaces deep face-to-face time with shallow likes and comments that don't build real trust.
expected_issues: turn 1 no position; turn 2 clear position achieved
avoid_behaviors: immediately piling on a new demand without consolidating

cases.name: Student needing the same scaffold repeatedly
cases.assignment: Argue whether students should choose their own books.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Persist patiently on one target across attempts.
cases.initial_draft: Books are good to read. Reading helps you learn things.
responses: I like reading books about dragons and space.
Reading is fun and my favorite books are long ones.
expected_issues: repeatedly avoids taking a position
avoid_behaviors: giving up and writing it for them

cases.name: Returning student showing increased independent control
cases.assignment: Argue whether AI should be allowed for homework.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Scaffold from prior developmental control; recognize independence.
cases.initial_draft: AI should be allowed for homework only as a tutor, not a ghostwriter, because a tool that explains builds skill while a tool that answers replaces it — and the difference is who does the thinking.
expected_issues: thesis already strong (per profile); support/explanation is the growth edge
avoid_behaviors: re-teaching the thesis the student already controls

cases.name: Ambiguous: both-sides could be a legitimate nuanced thesis
cases.assignment: Evaluate whether remote learning is effective.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Distinguish evasive 'both' from a genuine nuanced claim.
cases.initial_draft: Remote learning is effective for motivated, self-regulating students and ineffective for those who depend on external structure; its value is therefore not a property of the medium but of the match between medium and learner.
expected_issues: nuanced position may be adequate, not evasive
avoid_behaviors: forcing a single-side thesis onto a legitimate nuanced claim

cases.name: Ambiguous: reflective piece not needing a thesis
cases.assignment: Reflect on something a job taught you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Honor reflective purpose; meaning over thesis.
cases.initial_draft: The night shift taught me that calm isn't the absence of fear. I was terrified most nights, but I learned to do the next necessary thing anyway, and somehow that became its own kind of steadiness.
expected_issues: reflection; should not be forced into argument thesis

cases.name: Narrative — telling instead of showing
cases.assignment: Write a personal narrative about a moment that changed you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Help the writer render experience concretely for a reader.
cases.initial_draft: The day I moved schools was really scary and sad. I felt nervous and alone and I didn't know anyone. It was a hard time but I got through it.
expected_issues: abstract 'telling' with no concrete scene or sensory detail
cases.expected_primary_target: showing vs. telling — render one concrete moment
avoid_behaviors: writing the scene for the student
treating this like an argument needing a thesis

cases.name: Narrative — summary where a scene is needed
cases.assignment: Write a narrative about a conflict with someone close to you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Distinguish scene from summary; slow down the important beat.
cases.initial_draft: Over the next three years my brother and I fought constantly about everything and eventually we stopped talking, which was the worst part of my life.
expected_issues: compresses the emotional climax into summary; no scene
cases.expected_primary_target: pacing — expand the pivotal moment into a scene
avoid_behaviors: inventing plot details for the student
imposing essay structure on a narrative

cases.name: Descriptive — flat detail, no dominant impression
cases.assignment: Describe a place that matters to you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Guide selection of detail toward a unifying impression.
cases.initial_draft: My grandmother's kitchen has a table and some chairs. There is a stove and a window. The walls are yellow and there is a clock.
expected_issues: inventory of neutral details with no dominant impression or sensory life
cases.expected_primary_target: dominant impression — let detail serve a feeling/meaning

cases.name: Process / how-to — steps out of order and unclear
cases.assignment: Explain how to do something you know well, step by step.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Sequence and reader-usability of instructions.
cases.initial_draft: To make a paper airplane you fold it and then you throw it. First get paper. You have to make the wings even or it won't fly. Fold it in half.
expected_issues: steps out of logical sequence; a reader could not follow
cases.expected_primary_target: logical sequencing of steps for the reader
avoid_behaviors: numbering the steps for the student

cases.name: Compare/contrast — no organizing scheme
cases.assignment: Compare two approaches to reducing traffic in cities.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Choose an organizing structure that serves comparison.
cases.initial_draft: Congestion pricing charges drivers money. Public transit investment builds trains and buses. Congestion pricing can feel unfair. Buses are slow sometimes. Trains cost a lot to build.
expected_issues: details alternate randomly; no point-by-point or block structure
cases.expected_primary_target: organizing structure for comparison (point-by-point vs. block)
avoid_behaviors: choosing the structure for the student

cases.name: Cause/effect — correlation asserted as cause
cases.assignment: Explain a cause of a social trend you have observed.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Strengthen causal reasoning; test the logic of a claim.
cases.initial_draft: Teen anxiety rose at the same time smartphones became common, so smartphones are clearly the cause of the anxiety epidemic.
expected_issues: treats correlation as proven causation; no mechanism or alternative explanations
cases.expected_primary_target: causal reasoning — evidence of mechanism vs. correlation
avoid_behaviors: telling the student their claim is simply wrong

cases.name: Literary analysis — plot summary instead of a claim
cases.assignment: Write an analysis of how the author develops a theme in the story.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Move from retelling to interpretive claim about the text.
cases.initial_draft: In the story the boy finds a bird with a broken wing. He takes care of it. Then the bird dies at the end and he is sad. The author shows a lot of things happening.
expected_issues: summarizes plot; no interpretive claim about how theme is built
avoid_behaviors: naming the theme for the student

cases.name: Rhetorical analysis — describes what, not how
cases.assignment: Analyze how the author persuades their audience in the speech.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Analyze rhetorical strategy (how) rather than restating content (what).
cases.initial_draft: The speaker says we must act on climate change now. He says it is urgent and that future generations depend on us. He believes we can still fix it.
expected_issues: paraphrases the message; does not analyze the rhetorical means
cases.expected_primary_target: analyze rhetorical strategy (how the text works on the audience)
avoid_behaviors: naming the devices for the student

cases.name: Research synthesis — source dump, no synthesis
cases.assignment: Synthesize at least two sources to make a point about remote learning.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Integrate sources into the writer's own line of reasoning.
cases.initial_draft: Smith (2021) says remote learning hurts test scores. Jones (2022) says remote learning helps flexibility. Lee (2020) says results are mixed.
expected_issues: strings sources together with no synthesis or writer's claim
cases.expected_primary_target: synthesis — put sources in conversation to serve the writer's point

cases.name: Lab report — subjective register in methods
cases.assignment: Write the methods section of your lab report.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Honor scientific register: precise, replicable, objective.
cases.initial_draft: We did the experiment and it was pretty fun. We kind of heated the water up a lot and waited a while and then looked at what happened.
expected_issues: vague, subjective, non-replicable; wrong register for a methods section
avoid_behaviors: writing the methods for the student

cases.name: Persuasive letter — audience/tone mismatch
cases.assignment: Write a letter to your principal proposing a change.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Match tone and appeals to a specific audience.
cases.initial_draft: Hey, the lunch here is honestly terrible and everyone hates it, you should just fix it because it's so bad and unfair to us.
expected_issues: tone inappropriate for the audience; appeals unlikely to persuade a principal
cases.expected_primary_target: audience awareness — tone and appeals for this reader

cases.name: Op-ed — strong public-audience opening (restraint)
cases.assignment: Write an op-ed on a local issue for a general newspaper audience.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Recognize an effective public-audience hook and stance.
cases.initial_draft: Every morning, two thousand commuters idle on a bridge that was declared unsafe a decade ago. We keep calling it a budget problem. It is not a budget problem; it is a decision to treat their time and safety as expendable.
expected_issues: opening is strong for the genre and audience
cases.expected_primary_target: light / consolidate the effective public-audience move, then advance
avoid_behaviors: forcing an academic thesis format onto an op-ed

cases.name: Personal statement — cliché instead of authentic voice
cases.assignment: Draft your college personal statement about a formative experience.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Develop authentic, specific voice over generic cliché.
cases.initial_draft: Ever since I was a little kid I have always wanted to help people and make a difference in the world. Playing sports taught me teamwork, hard work, and never giving up.
expected_issues: generic clichés; no specific, authentic, revealing detail
cases.expected_primary_target: authentic voice via specific, revealing detail
avoid_behaviors: writing the anecdote for the student

cases.name: Business email — buries the purpose
cases.assignment: Write a short email asking a colleague to review a document by Friday.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Purpose-first, concise professional communication.
cases.initial_draft: Hi, I hope you are doing well and had a great weekend. Things have been really busy over here with a lot going on lately and I wanted to reach out about a few things that have been on my mind regarding the project we discussed.
expected_issues: request buried; reader can't find the ask or the deadline
cases.expected_primary_target: purpose-first structure — lead with the request and deadline

cases.name: Cover letter — claims without evidence
cases.assignment: Write a cover letter paragraph about your qualifications.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Support claims with concrete evidence of qualification.
cases.initial_draft: I am a hard worker, a great team player, and highly detail-oriented. I would be a perfect fit for this role and I am very passionate about the work.
expected_issues: asserts traits with no evidence a reader could verify

cases.name: Summary/precis — inserts opinion, loses fidelity
cases.assignment: Write an objective summary of the article.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Fidelity and concision proper to a summary; withhold opinion.
cases.initial_draft: The article talks about zoos. Honestly zoos are kind of cruel if you ask me. It says some zoos help endangered animals which I guess is good.
expected_issues: injects personal opinion; misrepresents the source's balance
cases.expected_primary_target: summary fidelity — represent the source, not the writer's opinion

cases.name: Annotated bibliography — describes, doesn't evaluate
cases.assignment: Write an annotation evaluating a source for your research project.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Evaluate a source's relevance/reliability, not just describe it.
cases.initial_draft: This article is about social media and mental health. It has a lot of information and statistics. The author wrote it in 2019. It is 12 pages long.
expected_issues: describes surface features; no evaluation of credibility or usefulness
cases.expected_primary_target: evaluation of the source (relevance/reliability) vs. description
avoid_behaviors: evaluating the source for the student

cases.name: Creative/poetry — do not impose essay logic
cases.assignment: Write a free-verse poem about a memory.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Honor the genre's resources (image, line, sound); do not essay-ify.
cases.initial_draft: the porch light / a moth against the screen / my father's cough in the next room / I pretend to be asleep
expected_issues: draft uses image and line effectively for the form
cases.expected_primary_target: light / consolidate the working images; invite the writer to develop by their own instinct
avoid_behaviors: imposing a thesis or paragraph structure on a poem

cases.name: Reflective portfolio — stops at events, no significance
cases.assignment: Reflect on what a semester project taught you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Move from recounting events to making meaning of them.
cases.initial_draft: First we picked a topic, then we did research, then we made the presentation, then we presented it to the class and got a good grade.
expected_issues: chronological recount with no reflection on significance/learning
cases.expected_primary_target: significance — what the experience means / what was learned
avoid_behaviors: forcing an argumentative thesis onto reflection

cases.name: Audience awareness — too technical for lay reader
cases.assignment: Explain your research to a general audience.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Adjust for a non-expert reader's knowledge.
cases.initial_draft: We employed a stochastic gradient descent optimizer with L2 regularization to minimize categorical cross-entropy across the held-out validation partition.
expected_issues: jargon dense; inaccessible to the stated general audience
cases.expected_primary_target: audience awareness — translate for a non-expert reader
avoid_behaviors: rewriting it in plain language for the student

cases.name: Tone inconsistency — casual in a formal task
cases.assignment: Write a formal analytical essay on economic inequality.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Consistency of register with task and audience.
cases.initial_draft: Economic inequality is a serious structural problem. But honestly the rich just kinda hoard everything lol and it's super messed up if you think about it.
expected_issues: register lurches from formal to casual mid-paragraph
cases.expected_primary_target: tone/register consistency for a formal essay

cases.name: Vague diction — 'things' and 'stuff'
cases.assignment: Explain why a hobby is important to you.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Precise word choice that carries meaning.
cases.initial_draft: Playing music is a good thing because it helps with stuff and makes things better and you learn a lot of things from doing it.
expected_issues: placeholder nouns ('things','stuff') carry no meaning
cases.expected_primary_target: precise diction — name what the vague words stand for

cases.name: Sentence variety — choppy monotony
cases.assignment: Write a narrative paragraph about a busy morning.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Sentence variety to control rhythm and emphasis.
cases.initial_draft: I woke up. I was late. I ran downstairs. I grabbed toast. I missed the bus. I was mad. I walked to school. I got there late.
expected_issues: uniform short simple sentences; monotonous rhythm
cases.expected_primary_target: sentence variety — combine/vary for rhythm and emphasis
avoid_behaviors: combining the sentences for the student

cases.name: Cohesion — paragraphs don't connect
cases.assignment: Argue for stronger public libraries.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Connective tissue between ideas/paragraphs.
cases.initial_draft: Libraries provide internet access to people without it. Libraries hold community events. Some libraries are old buildings. Funding for libraries has dropped.
expected_issues: true statements sit in isolation; no logical connection between them
cases.expected_primary_target: cohesion — show how the ideas relate and build

cases.name: Counterargument absent in an argument
cases.assignment: Argue whether cities should ban cars downtown.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Anticipate and engage opposing views.
cases.initial_draft: Cities should ban cars downtown because it reduces pollution, makes streets safer, and encourages walking. These are all clearly good things for everyone.
expected_issues: one-sided; never acknowledges or answers opposing concerns
cases.expected_primary_target: counterargument — engage a serious opposing view

cases.name: Concession is a straw man
cases.assignment: Argue for a four-day school week.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Represent opposing views fairly before responding.
cases.initial_draft: Some people think a four-day week is bad, but they just don't care about students being happy, so they are obviously wrong.
expected_issues: opposing view distorted into a straw man; not fairly represented
cases.expected_primary_target: fair representation of the opposing view before rebutting
avoid_behaviors: supplying a fair version of the opposing view

cases.name: Conclusion introduces a new argument
cases.assignment: Conclude your essay on renewable energy.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Function of a conclusion vs. opening new lines of argument.
cases.initial_draft: In conclusion, renewable energy is important. Also, nuclear power is actually the best solution and we should build many new reactors immediately for a totally different reason.
expected_issues: introduces a brand-new claim in the conclusion
cases.expected_primary_target: function of a conclusion (synthesize, not open new arguments)

cases.name: Wordiness / padding
cases.assignment: Write a concise argument paragraph.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Conciseness — cut padding without losing meaning.
cases.initial_draft: Due to the fact that in this day and age it is basically very much true that most people generally tend to believe that exercise is something that is good for them, it can be said that fitness is important.
expected_issues: heavy padding and filler; one idea inflated to a long sentence
cases.expected_primary_target: conciseness — cut filler while keeping the idea

cases.name: Quote dropped in without attribution/integration
cases.assignment: Use a quotation from the text to support your point.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Integrate and frame evidence (signal phrase, attribution).
cases.initial_draft: The character is lonely. "The house was empty and the phone never rang." This shows loneliness in the story.
expected_issues: quote dropped in with no signal phrase, framing, or attribution
cases.expected_primary_target: integrating evidence — frame and attribute the quotation

cases.name: Faulty parallelism in a series
cases.assignment: Write about the benefits of volunteering.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Parallel structure in coordinated series.
cases.initial_draft: Volunteering helps you meet people, learning new skills, and it builds your confidence.
expected_issues: items in the series are not grammatically parallel

cases.name: Point-of-view shifting (you/one/I)
cases.assignment: Write about how to manage stress.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Consistent point of view across the paragraph.
cases.initial_draft: When I feel stressed, you should take a walk, and one can also try breathing exercises so that we feel calmer.
expected_issues: pronoun/POV shifts among I, you, one, we in one sentence
avoid_behaviors: choosing the POV for the student

cases.name: Multilingual writer — surface errors, strong idea
cases.assignment: Argue whether homework should be graded.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Prioritize the highest-leverage move; honor strong meaning over surface errors.
cases.initial_draft: Homework should not be graded because it is the place where student make the mistake and learn from it; if we grade the practice, student become afraid to try and the learning is stop.
expected_issues: minor article/agreement errors, but the argument is genuinely strong and clear
cases.expected_primary_target: consolidate the strong reasoning / advance the argument (do not fixate on surface grammar)
avoid_behaviors: correcting the grammar for the student
reducing a strong idea to an error hunt

cases.name: Student pastes AI-generated text and asks 'is this good?'
cases.assignment: Write your own argument about urban green space.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Preserve authorship; return the thinking to the student.
cases.initial_draft: Here's my intro, is this good? 'Urban green spaces represent a multifaceted nexus of ecological, psychological, and socioeconomic benefits that municipalities must holistically prioritize in contemporary urban planning paradigms.'
expected_issues: text is not the student's own thinking; authorship at risk
cases.expected_primary_target: return authorship — get the student articulating their own point in their own words
avoid_behaviors: evaluating it as if it were the student's developed thinking

cases.name: Perfectionist stuck — won't commit anything
cases.assignment: Draft an argument about standardized testing.
cases.pedagogical_purpose: Unblock action; lower the stakes to get words down.
